claims.text: Grants cover tuition fees for students from low-income households.
Grants are for students ineligible for Scottish Government tuition fee support.
Grants are available for students returning to study after withdrawing.
Grants are available for asylum seekers.
The application portal opens on June 1, 2026.
The application portal closes at 5pm on December 1, 2026.
The grants are for the academic year 2026-27.
The grants cover tuition fees up to £1,820 per year.
Applicants must demonstrate that their financial circumstances do not allow them to cover tuition fees.
Retrospective applications will not be accepted.
Applications will not be accepted if the student has incurred tuition fee debts in a previous year and cannot progress.
Applicants must live in a low-income household.

Applicants must be ordinarily resident in Scotland and have completed at least two years of secondary schooling or college education in Scotland, OR demonstrate a substantial and recent connection to Scotland.
Applicants must be entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, have Limited Leave to Remain valid for the entire course duration, or be an asylum seeker.
Applicants must not be eligible for public funds towards tuition fees.
Applicants must not have already graduated with a university degree, with exceptions for second degrees under specific criteria.
Applicants eligible for SAAS/Student Loans Company maintenance loans are expected to use them fully.
CEF will not consider applications if the student is eligible for support from Student Finance England, Wales, or Northern Ireland, or any loan/grant from an overseas government/agency.
CEF generally will not fund more than one repeat year.
Applications from students who previously received funding for one undergraduate degree and wish to start a different course may not be considered.
Part-time students receiving SAAS tuition fee support and no other grants/loans may apply if the SAAS award is less than total fees.
Students who came to Scotland solely to study at university/college without prior ties to Scotland are not eligible.
Applications from students who already have a university degree may be considered exceptionally at CEF's discretion.

Applicants must have an unconditional offer for, or be a continuing student on, a full-time, part-time, or distance learning undergraduate degree course in academic year 2026-27 at a Scottish Higher Education Institution or a course validated by one.
HNC, HND, Access courses, Accelerated degree courses with graduate entry, courses outside Scotland, Open University courses, CPD courses, and university courses below degree level are not eligible.
Postgraduate degrees are not eligible.
CEF has a budget to fund students who completed an undergraduate degree in the past and wish to start a new undergraduate degree in a different field in academic year 2026-27.
Students seeking a second degree must have completed their first degree at least two years before the start of their new course.
Students seeking a second degree must enter the first year of their new course in academic year 2026-27.
Students seeking a second degree must have been unable to gain employment in their previous field, be unemployed, or facing redundancy.
Students seeking a second degree must wish to reskill in a different field recognized as a skills shortage area for the Scottish economy.
Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.
Applicants must take full advantage of SAAS/Student Loans Company loans.
No exceptions or exemptions will be made to eligibility criteria.
Students who have already started a second degree before academic year 2026-27 are not eligible.
The awards cover tuition fees only.
Household gross income thresholds are used as guides, not hard cut-offs.
Student living cost loans or social benefits are not considered part of total household income.
Applications are considered on a case-by-case basis, taking into account household income and extenuating circumstances.
All applications are made online.
An eligibility checker should be completed before applying.
The application form is only accessible during the application window.
An automatic reply confirms receipt of a complete application.
Late applications will not be accepted unless the student was informed of SAAS ineligibility after the portal closed.
Applicants will be notified of the outcome within two to three weeks if all information and referee responses are timely.
Applicants will be notified of the outcome via email.
Supporting documents include evidence of eligibility, university acceptance letter, SAAS Award Notice, and P60/pay slips/Universal Credit statements.
Students receiving a SAAS bursary must provide a copy of their SAAS award letter.
Supporting evidence can be submitted as scanned copies or mobile images.
There is a 5MB size limit per file for uploaded documents.
